components.name: Syntax
components.plain: Reads Mapal source text and gives back tokens, a parse tree and error messages. It also formats source files.

transformations.name: lex
transformations.plain: Cuts the text into tokens. It is total: unknown input becomes an Error token plus a diagnostic and scanning goes on; guard arrows are single tokens recognised by adjacency and statement-start context.
transformations.lives: compiler heap; runs once per source on the main thread

transformations.name: parse
transformations.plain: Builds the parse tree from the tokens by recursive descent, recovering at statement and item borders. It merges lexer and parser errors and sorts them by position.
transformations.lives: compiler heap; recursion depth capped by DEPTH_LIMIT so deep nesting reports an error instead of overflowing the stack

transformations.name: format_source
transformations.plain: Re-prints source in the one canonical layout (four spaces, multiline braces) by walking the token stream and re-spacing it, keeping comments. It refuses input that has syntax errors.
transformations.lives: compiler heap: output String; used by `mapal fmt` and the editors' format action

transformations.name: source to tree
transformations.plain: The two steps above in order: lex then parse.

patterns.name: Hand-written recursive-descent parser with depth limit
patterns.plain: One function per grammar rule, a cursor over the token array, and a recursion cap that turns runaway nesting into an error.

patterns.name: Error recovery with cooldown
patterns.plain: After an error the parser skips to a safe point and mutes follow-up errors for a short while.

patterns.name: Context-sensitive guard-arrow scan
patterns.plain: A guard arrow like -42-> is one lexeme only when adjacent and at statement start; otherwise it is minus, number, arrow.

patterns.name: Spans instead of copied text
patterns.plain: Tokens and names hold only offsets, and text is cut from the one source string when needed.

patterns.name: Line-start index with binary search
patterns.plain: Line starts are stored once, and an offset is found by search.

patterns.name: Token-stream pretty printer
patterns.plain: The formatter walks tokens, tracks a stack of brace frames and decides spacing and line breaks from neighbouring token kinds.

patterns.name: Renderer-free diagnostics
patterns.plain: Diagnostics are plain data with no Display; only the CLI and the language server turn them into text or editor messages.

components.name: Lowering
components.plain: Turns the parse tree into the Flow graph: it resolves names, works out types and sizes, and builds the graph.

transformations.name: lower: Syntax -> Flow
transformations.plain: The whole component as one partial map: each parse-tree form goes to its graph realization, or to a diagnostic where the form is outside the core language. Entry point; handles programs with top-level values by first computing them.

transformations.name: collect top-level values
transformations.plain: Finds top-level bindings, who reads whom, and rejects effects or cycles among them.

transformations.name: compute top-level values before the program runs
transformations.plain: Lowers a small synthetic program and runs its top-level scalars on the interpreter, so they become literals/sizes.
transformations.lives: compiler heap; uses the interpreter and a work budget

transformations.name: lower with globals
transformations.plain: The staged pipeline: structural checks, types, effects, signatures, then monomorphization rounds of typing + emission + seal.

transformations.name: effect analysis
transformations.plain: Walks the call graph to mark effectful functions and reports recursion.

transformations.name: build the type table
transformations.plain: Resolves every declared type, rejecting cycles, bad sizes and duplicates.

transformations.name: build function signatures
transformations.plain: Gives every function its declared signature, flagged effectful or generic.

transformations.name: typing and size inference
transformations.plain: Per function (or generic instance): types literals by unification, infers sizes and formats of generic calls, computes captures, and records which instances are needed.

transformations.name: type one function
transformations.plain: Walks a function, unifies literal widths, types map/fold blocks and computes their captures.
transformations.lives: compiler heap; WTy variables and union-find per function

transformations.name: infer generic sizes and formats
transformations.plain: Solves the size equations of a generic call to choose its instance.

transformations.name: declare, emit and seal
transformations.plain: Declares each function and body, emits statements and chains through the IR builder, then seals the graph.

transformations.name: emit one function
transformations.plain: Binds parameters, threads the IO token for effectful functions, emits the body and return, fail-fast on the first error.

transformations.name: prove widen exactness
transformations.plain: After sealing, uses the facts to check that each int-to-f32 widen stays within the exact range.
transformations.lives: compiler heap; reads facts stored on the sealed graph

patterns.name: Staged pipeline with fail-fast emission
patterns.plain: Checks run in stages and are collected; once emission starts the first error stops that function.

patterns.name: Fixed-point rounds (monomorphization)
patterns.plain: Repeat typing and emission up to 32 rounds until every called generic instance was declared.

patterns.name: Union-find over literal types
patterns.plain: Integer/float literals of unknown width are variables merged into groups, then pinned to a type.

patterns.name: Size equation solving (inversion, monotone search, divisor enumeration)
patterns.plain: Solves expressions like n*2 = 8 for n by inverting or searching.

patterns.name: Cycle detection by iterative DFS
patterns.plain: Finds recursive types and recursive calls with an explicit stack frame.

patterns.name: Scope stack with poison marks
patterns.plain: Lexical scopes as a stack, with names marked unreadable after a loop.

patterns.name: Token threading for effects
patterns.plain: Effectful functions take and return an IO token so order of print/clock is explicit data.

patterns.name: Capture analysis (struct captures flattened to fields)
patterns.plain: Finds which outer values a map/fold body reads and passes them as leading inputs.

patterns.name: Prelude of parsed conversion signatures
patterns.plain: to/widen are declared as ordinary generic functions in a prelude parsed once; calls are realized by the builtin the format pair admits.

patterns.name: Typed diagnostic catalogue
patterns.plain: Every error is one LCode variant with a stable code string.

components.name: Checker
components.plain: Checks rules the Flow graph must follow after lowering (one return value, no effects racing each other).

transformations.name: check
transformations.plain: Takes the sealed flow graph, the parse tree and the source, runs both passes, and returns a list of errors; an empty list means accept. No HashMap is used, so the same input always gives the same list.
transformations.lives: compiler heap; the result is a Vec<Diagnostic>

transformations.name: return exclusivity pass
transformations.plain: For every function in the flow graph, counts the writers feeding its return value; each beyond the first becomes T0101 at the writing operation's location.
transformations.lives: reads the sealed CategoryIr on the compiler heap

transformations.name: effect legality pass
transformations.plain: Walks the parse tree; inside a parallel fan-out branch, any print, clock read or file read becomes T0201. A nested sequential block stays inside the illegal zone.
transformations.lives: compiler heap: a Walk with a Scope stack

patterns.name: Tree walk keyed by node kind with sticky context
patterns.plain: A fan-out opens the illegal context, and a sequential block inside it inherits it.

patterns.name: Lexical scope stack
patterns.plain: Push on entering a block, pop on leaving, to know whether a name is a local binding.

patterns.name: In-edge count on the graph
patterns.plain: Counts non-pair edges into the return object to find a second writer.

patterns.name: Deterministic ordering
patterns.plain: No hash maps; findings come in a fixed order so two runs agree exactly.

components.name: Flow graph
components.plain: The one data structure every later stage shares: Mapal's types and the dataflow graph, with its builder, validator and pictures.

transformations.name: IrBuilder (declare, build_fn, FnBuilder ops, seal)
transformations.plain: The only way to make a graph: one method per operation that checks types and shape rules and refuses ill-formed edges, then seal freezes it. Called by the lowering stage.
transformations.lives: builder holds growing SlotMaps on the compiler heap; seal moves them into CategoryIr and creates the empty Facts

transformations.name: FnBuilder primitives (constant, pack, binop, phi, map, fold, begin_loop/loop_back/loop_exit, output, read)
transformations.plain: Each call appends an object and edge; rejection matrix is IrError.

transformations.name: seal
transformations.plain: Freeze: global checks then immutable graph.

transformations.name: validate
transformations.plain: An independent re-check of every graph rule (ownership, edge types, tokens, loops, references); used as the test oracle.

transformations.name: fact queries (tile_plan, loop_plan, last_use_plan, path_plan, precision_plan, elem_plan, access_plan, residence_plan, ...)
transformations.plain: Each query reads the sealed graph and the facts it depends on and stores its answer once on the graph.
transformations.lives: cached in CategoryIr.facts OnceLock slots; per-function

transformations.name: sccs / topo_order / loop_structure
transformations.plain: Find the cycles (loops) and a legal execution order, without recursion.

transformations.name: to_mermaid / to_mermaid_flow / to_mermaid_category / to_mermaid_string
transformations.plain: Three views of the graph (flow, category, string diagram), each condensed or full, printed as Mermaid.

transformations.name: category_diagram
transformations.plain: Objects as boxes and morphisms as labelled arrows.

transformations.name: string_diagram
transformations.plain: String-diagram view (wires and boxes).

transformations.name: lint_mermaid
transformations.plain: Check that Mermaid text will render.

transformations.name: math candidates / admits / choose
transformations.plain: For a builtin and a target's available units, list realizations, admit those within the stated error, pick the cheapest by cost, never by target name.
transformations.lives: compiler heap, decided at compile time; Choice later printed by a backend

transformations.name: Trace (record a reference definition as data)
transformations.plain: The reference definition of exp/sqrt/sin/cos is written once over plain operations; running it with Trace records the steps so a backend can print them, running it with Native computes numbers.
transformations.lives: Vec<Step> on compiler heap; printed as LLVM text or C

transformations.name: read::load / decode / encode
transformations.plain: Load a binary file as an array of the declared element type, with exact-size checks and friendly messages.
transformations.lives: file bytes into a Vec<u8> then Vec<Value> on host heap

transformations.name: unit_plan / out_rows
transformations.plain: Group sites into row blocks and colour on-chip buffers by death.

patterns.name: Arena with typed ids (slotmap)
patterns.plain: Objects, morphisms and functions live in slot arenas; a typed id cannot be confused with another kind, and side tables are SecondaryMaps keyed by the same id.

patterns.name: Gatekeeper builder + sealing (ill-formed is unconstructible)
patterns.plain: The only mutable form is IrBuilder; sealing returns an immutable graph, and an independent validator double-checks.

patterns.name: Fact cache stored on the sealed graph (compute once, read after)
patterns.plain: One OnceLock per fact and function; dependent facts read stored inputs; never recomputed per call site.

patterns.name: Iterative Tarjan strongly connected components
patterns.plain: Finds loops as cycles with an explicit work stack, no recursion.

patterns.name: Kahn topological order
patterns.plain: A legal order of operations by a worklist, with loop back edges cut.

patterns.name: Deterministic containers (no HashMap)
patterns.plain: Insertion-ordered Vecs and slot maps so dumps, orders and snapshots are byte-stable.

patterns.name: Depth guard on types
patterns.plain: Type walks are iterative or capped at 64 levels so a hostile deep type cannot overflow the stack.

patterns.name: Definition as data (tagless-final Arith trait: run or record)
patterns.plain: One generic definition of exp/sqrt/sin/cos runs natively (interpreter) or is traced into steps a backend prints.

patterns.name: Cost-based choice over declared units
patterns.plain: Realizations are data (Unit, TargetDef) filtered by error bound and ranked by issue cost.

patterns.name: Forward error analysis (gamma, bound_coef)
patterns.plain: A-priori rounding error of a sum of products, per site and per precision member.

patterns.name: Lifetime colouring of buffers
patterns.plain: Values that die before another is born share a colour (a buffer).

patterns.name: Plain-function rendering, no Display
patterns.plain: Values stay free of printing code; text comes from plain functions like ty_label.

components.name: Facts
components.plain: Computes, once per graph, what is true of it (loops, lifetimes, tiles, bounds, ...). Every later decision reads these facts.

transformations.name: Seal the graph
transformations.plain: Freezes the builder's graph and pre-allocates one empty fact slot per function.

transformations.name: Validate the graph
transformations.plain: Independently re-checks the graph's shape rules and lists violations; the test oracle for every pass.

transformations.name: Loop facts
transformations.plain: Finds cycles, orders the graph, and reads each loop's canonical shape, trip splits and per-trip array writes.

transformations.name: sccs
transformations.plain: Strongly connected sets of objects, which are the loops.

transformations.name: topo_order
transformations.plain: A deterministic evaluation order of a function's operations.

transformations.name: loop_structure
transformations.plain: Lists each loop and its merge objects.

transformations.name: loop_plan
transformations.plain: Names init, back route, exit and the decide/advance order of each canonical loop.

transformations.name: trip_split
transformations.plain: Cuts a counted loop's trips where guards on the counter change behaviour.

transformations.name: write_delta
transformations.plain: The contiguous rows or pieces of a carried array that each trip writes.

transformations.name: unchanged_plan and call_keep
transformations.plain: Carries write deltas through row-local maps to say what stays the same between trips and calls.

transformations.name: static_plan
transformations.plain: Finds values computable before the program runs and prices embedding them against computing them.

transformations.name: Lifetime and emission facts
transformations.plain: Which values need bytes, when each dies, which bytes each operation touches, and where bytes live.

transformations.name: emission_plan
transformations.plain: Classifies each object as materialized, dissolved into a view, inline or named.

transformations.name: last_use_plan
transformations.plain: Positions, death points, escapes and loop-carried liveness over two iterations.

transformations.name: access_plan
transformations.plain: Reads, writes, storage classes and hazard edges per loop trip.

transformations.name: residence_plan
transformations.plain: Peak live bytes from producer to last reader, compared to a cache size.

transformations.name: path_plan and guard_plan
transformations.plain: Splits work into independent tasks, finds host checkpoints, and records which conditional arms must be gated.

transformations.name: bounds_proof and finite_plan
transformations.plain: Proves indices in range and values finite using integer and float interval arithmetic narrowed by the conditions that hold where a value is used.

transformations.name: Site recognition
transformations.plain: Recognizes maps and folds as tiles, row folds, cells and data moves and gives each element as a closed function of its index.

transformations.name: elem_plan and map_law
transformations.plain: Each array element as a closed function of its index, piecewise where cells outside a range are a capture's own.

transformations.name: tile_plan and variants
transformations.plain: Finds sum-of-products sites: plain, strided, with epilogue, narrow-storage, and mixed-radix.

transformations.name: radix_plan
transformations.plain: Writes each integer value as digits of the inputs so strided and implicit-matrix reads are visible.

transformations.name: cell_plan, row_fold, whole_fold, move_plan, footprint_plan
transformations.plain: Per-cell maps, row folds, data-move sites and what each cell reads.

transformations.name: Arithmetic freedom facts
transformations.plain: States what the arithmetic may become: fused multiply-add, regrouped folds, block-combined folds.

transformations.name: step_algebra
transformations.plain: Multiply-add pairs that can fuse and fold steps that can regroup.

transformations.name: fold_combine
transformations.plain: How block partials of a fold combine and how each per-row value is applied.

transformations.name: precision_plan
transformations.plain: Admitted product precisions, where rounding happens once, and a-priori error bounds per site.

transformations.name: Row-block and streaming facts
transformations.plain: Groups sites that can share a block of rows on chip, then proves a group can run window by window in one pass.

transformations.name: unit_plan
transformations.plain: Row-block groups with row-closed edges and bytes per row.

transformations.name: stream_plan
transformations.plain: One-pass windowed evaluation of an axis, with mask boxes and per-fold combine laws.

patterns.name: Fact cache on the sealed graph
patterns.plain: Each query is a pure function of the sealed graph, computed once into a write-once slot and read after that.

patterns.name: Arena with typed ids
patterns.plain: Objects, morphisms and functions sit in slot maps keyed by distinct id types; secondary maps hang per-id data off them with deterministic order.

patterns.name: Strongly connected components
patterns.plain: Loop detection by finding cycles in the object graph.

patterns.name: Topological order
patterns.plain: Evaluation order with insertion-order tie-breaks.

patterns.name: Liveness with two-iteration loop carry
patterns.plain: Positions and death points of values, with a value live across a loop back edge marked carried.

patterns.name: Interval analysis narrowed by conditions
patterns.plain: Integer and float ranges tightened by the guards, loop bounds and phi arms where a value is used.

patterns.name: Digit decomposition of indices
patterns.plain: Index arithmetic with constant division and remainder is split into per-digit affine terms to detect implicit matrix products.

patterns.name: Hazard classification (RAW/WAR/WAW)
patterns.plain: Dependencies between operations from the bytes they read and write, with shared buffers.

patterns.name: Working-set peak over a live interval
patterns.plain: A value's residence from the peak live bytes between producer and last reader against cache size.

patterns.name: A-priori error bound (gamma-n)
patterns.plain: A closed-form rounding error bound for sums of products used as the correctness gate.

patterns.name: Online combine (running max and rescale)
patterns.plain: Per-block partials combined by the fold's own operator, with exp rescale for a running max.

patterns.name: Independent validator
patterns.plain: A second pass re-derives the graph invariants without sharing builder code.

patterns.name: Fact arms (OFF switches)
patterns.plain: Each rule can be switched off for comparison, never per hardware.

components.name: Rewrites
components.plain: Rewrites the Flow graph into an equal, cheaper one (fold constants, remove dead and repeated work, inline, unroll).

transformations.name: rewrite: the fixpoint pipeline
transformations.plain: Runs inline, unroll, lift, constant fold, CSE, DCE and map fusion round after round until nothing changes (at most 32 rounds); the identity on non-canonical loops.
transformations.lives: compiler heap; returns a new graph

transformations.name: Analysis passes
transformations.plain: Each pass reads the graph and fills plan channels without changing the graph.

transformations.name: Constant folding and identities
transformations.plain: Folds constant scalars and forwards identities at the oracle's exact semantics, never folding a trap.

transformations.name: Common-subexpression elimination
transformations.plain: Merges duplicate pure computations; an element view outside guard arms is keyed by constant index value.

transformations.name: Dead-code elimination
transformations.plain: Drops dead cones of pure, non-trapping, terminating operations.

transformations.name: Map fusion
transformations.plain: Replaces map g after map f by one map, and drops map of identity.

transformations.name: Inlining
transformations.plain: Strips Call operations by substituting the callee's body when it is small enough (256 morphisms).

transformations.name: Loop lifting
transformations.plain: Recognizes counted accumulator and fill loops and rewrites them as captured Fold or Map.

transformations.name: Loop unrolling
transformations.plain: Replays a short constant-trip loop as its trips one after another, up to 128 trips.

transformations.name: Static folding
transformations.plain: Computes the static_plan roots with the interpreter and replaces their cones with constants.
transformations.lives: compiler heap; interpreter run at compile time

transformations.name: Replay
transformations.plain: Walks each function in topological order, classifies each object by its recipe, and rebuilds an equivalent graph through the public builder, so the output is well-formed by construction.

transformations.name: Canonical-loop guard
transformations.plain: If any loop is outside the canonical shapes, rewrite hands the graph back untouched.

patterns.name: Plan then replay
patterns.plain: Every pass only decides (graph to plan, pure); one shared replayer is the only code that builds graphs.

patterns.name: Fixpoint iteration with round cap
patterns.plain: Rounds repeat until all plans are empty or 32 rounds, with validation after each rebuild.

patterns.name: Value-numbering CSE
patterns.plain: Operations with the same op and same source are merged; views key by constant index value outside guard arms.

patterns.name: Liveness-based DCE
patterns.plain: Backward reachability from outputs and effects; anything that may trap or diverge is pinned live.

patterns.name: Functor law as rewrite rule
patterns.plain: Map fusion justified by map g after map f equals map (g after f); each pass names its law and preconditions.

patterns.name: Body substitution (inlining and fusion synthesis)
patterns.plain: A callee or fused body is rebuilt in the caller with its input mapped to the call source and fresh ids.

patterns.name: Evaluate at compile time with the oracle
patterns.plain: Static values are computed by the interpreter itself, so they are exact on every number face.

patterns.name: By-value intake and no-op shortcut
patterns.plain: The graph is moved in; an all-empty round returns it without a rebuild.

patterns.name: Random program generator (testgen)
patterns.plain: A proptest script of steps is built into a sealed graph or source text, used to validate rules on programs they were not designed on; checked in parallel.

patterns.name: Rule data table
patterns.plain: The Zip/Enumerate naturality laws kept as a const table.

components.name: Interpreter
components.plain: Runs a Flow graph directly on the CPU. It is the reference: every compiled result is compared against it.

transformations.name: run / run_ordered
transformations.plain: Seed the entry function (world token or unit), walk the graph, return the outcome and output; total, never panics.
transformations.lives: compiler heap; fuel is a u64 counter passed by &mut

transformations.name: eval_fn_within (walk operations in topological order)
transformations.plain: For each morphism in order compute the target value from its sources; Map and Fold call body functions; reads load files; each step spends one unit of fuel.

transformations.name: run_loop (guard-first loop driver)
transformations.plain: Per trip: decide and exit first, advance only if continuing, so speculative reads never happen on the exit step.
transformations.lives: EvalCtx.env, staging buffers reset per trip

transformations.name: Phi handler (gated arms)
transformations.plain: Arm work that may trap or is heavy runs only when the condition picks that arm.

transformations.name: eval_values / eval_values_once / static_cone
transformations.plain: Evaluate only the cone of values feeding chosen root objects; used to embed compile-time constants.
transformations.lives: SecondaryMap of the wanted objects; results Vec<Option<RValue>>

transformations.name: run_bound (record tape, reverse sweep)
transformations.plain: Run exactly, record each float op, then one backward pass per printed value gives how far fast realizations may differ (reduced-precision members, summation order, fma, math builtins).

transformations.name: run_weakest
transformations.plain: Run with every admitted reduced-precision multiply taken at its coarsest grid, giving the opposite extreme of the oracle.

transformations.name: Math and Narrow ops via ir Native Arith
transformations.plain: Evaluate exp/sqrt/sin/cos and narrow rounding with the same definitions a backend prints.

patterns.name: Fuel (step budget) for total evaluation
patterns.plain: A u64 budget decremented per step so every run halts with Done, Diverged or Trapped.

patterns.name: Result as early-exit channel (Abort)
patterns.plain: Traps, divergence and read failure travel as Err and are lifted once at the entry.

patterns.name: Guard-first loop evaluation
patterns.plain: Decide and exit cone evaluated before the advance cone.

patterns.name: Reverse-mode derivative tape (first-order error composition)
patterns.plain: Record partial derivatives forward, sweep backward per output to compose deviations along the program.

patterns.name: Shared immutable arrays (Rc) with staging slots for products
patterns.plain: Arrays are reference counted; products are assembled in staging buffers slot by slot, matching Pair edges.

patterns.name: Cone evaluation (evaluate only what a root reads)
patterns.plain: Restrict the walk to the set of objects feeding wanted roots.

patterns.name: Thread-local recorders (tape, weakest flag, read failure)
patterns.plain: Optional modes switched by scoped thread-local state so the common path has no extra parameters.

components.name: Hardware facts and rules
components.plain: Describes a chip by its measurable properties and picks optimization switches from those properties, never from a chip's name.

transformations.name: Calibration probes
transformations.plain: Small CUDA programs time the chip (latency, bandwidth, matrix rate, launch gaps, L2 keep, efficiency curves, primitive rates) and print name=value lines. A Python script turns the print-out into calibration keys and Rust table fields.
transformations.lives: runs on the GPU box; output is a text file on disk; extra probe in benches/local/place_calib.cu, optional modules in benches/local/place_calib_opt.cu, driver script benches/local/place_calib.sh, converter benches/local/place_calib_facts.py

transformations.name: Native GPU profile
transformations.plain: Query the driver, find the calibration line, and assemble the part's profile. No part names are looked at.
transformations.lives: compiler process: one TargetProfile leaked into a OnceLock static at first use

transformations.name: Ask the driver
transformations.plain: Loads libcuda.so.1 at run time and reads attributes.

transformations.name: Find the calibration
transformations.plain: Env file, cache file, committed line in that order.
transformations.lives: reads a file from disk; text kept in the process

transformations.name: Assemble the profile
transformations.plain: Fills Gpu, Caps and DeviceCost; fills the PlaceFacts fields from the calibration's place.* keys.

transformations.name: Choose optimization switches from properties
transformations.plain: Maps a chip and a site's fill to the switches, using thresholds that sit between the nearest measured winner and loser.
transformations.lives: compiler process, pure function evaluated per site while emitting

patterns.name: Facts carry provenance
patterns.plain: Every number is tagged with how it was obtained, and uncertain ones are marked so a decision that depends on them can be called open.

patterns.name: Layered fallback for calibration
patterns.plain: Try the user's file, then the file in the repository, else run with unmeasured numbers.

patterns.name: Capabilities as geometry
patterns.plain: Instructions are described by what they move and compute, so rules never compare versions.

patterns.name: Probe sweep to knee
patterns.plain: Each primitive is swept over how much work a unit keeps in flight; rate is the best point, concurrency the least in flight reaching 90 percent of it.

patterns.name: Static table per part
patterns.plain: A constant struct per known part, plus a lookup by physical key for new ones.

patterns.name: Threshold between nearest winner and loser
patterns.plain: Each rule's cut is placed between the closest measured case that won and the closest that lost, then replayed.

patterns.name: Plan and replay
patterns.plain: Decisions are stored as data (a tsv of measurements) and a test replays them against the rule code.

patterns.name: ON/OFF measurement arms
patterns.plain: Every optimization switch can be forced on or off from the command line for A/B timing; defaults come from the rules only.

components.name: Machine model
components.plain: A model of one machine that prices a way of running a computation and searches for the cheapest, with a bridge to the GPU backend.

transformations.name: Generate candidate schedules
transformations.plain: From the machine's facts and the site, list operations, then tiles, then traversals, never from a fixed table.

transformations.name: Price a schedule
transformations.plain: One evaluator for every schedule: steady state of a trip, a wave's pipeline, the grid by traversal, plus fixed costs. Reads only measured or declared facts.

transformations.name: A trip's steady state
transformations.plain: The slowest of compute, issue, scratchpad, and every mover; a mover with too little in flight is slowed by Little's law.

transformations.name: Pipeline calculation
transformations.plain: fill + trips x (slowest of compute and movement + barriers) + drain.

transformations.name: Count misses by distinct bytes
transformations.plain: Closed forms for lockstep waves, walks and staggered starts, counting distinct slices rather than bytes requested.
transformations.lives: compiler process; memoized in thread-local hash maps

transformations.name: Zero pass, reduce, launches
transformations.plain: Costs outside the loop: zeroing the output, workspace reduce, launches.

transformations.name: Admissible floor
transformations.plain: The same evaluation with every operand byte missed exactly once, cheap and never above the true price; used to cut the search.

transformations.name: Evaluate at every corner
transformations.plain: Prices a candidate with each fact group at its slow or fast end, sixteen times.

transformations.name: Branch and bound search
transformations.plain: Walks coordinate prefixes in a fixed order and cuts any prefix whose admissible bound is worse than the k-th best so far; the best go through a gate, then are priced at every corner and the minimax pick is taken.
transformations.lives: compiler process; Best keeps a bounded top list

transformations.name: Tile bound
transformations.plain: Cheapest any schedule with this slot tile can be: peak compute and the panel stream.

transformations.name: Point bound
transformations.plain: Compute at the efficiency this footprint's occupancy reaches.

transformations.name: Post-lowering gate
transformations.plain: Checks the candidate actually lowers to code (and, with an arm, assembles without spills); a refusal makes the next candidate be taken. The gate itself is a closure supplied by the backend.

transformations.name: Minimax verdict
from: Machine: times per candidate at value
transformations.plain: Picks the candidate whose worst regret over the corners is least; marks the pick open on a flip at a corner or a tie within the null.

transformations.name: Translate the profile
transformations.plain: Executors, places, capacity groups, resources, pipes, operation rows, movers, dispatch and measured primitives built from the profile; each number keeps its provenance and every missing one is marked.
transformations.lives: compiler process heap; cached per part in a thread-local MACHINES map

transformations.name: Place one site
transformations.plain: Translates the site, lists the emitters as lowerings, sets the rules' launch as incumbent, runs the search with the post-lowering gate, and records the pick and a ; mapal.place line. When the best does not clear the band, the rules' launch is kept; when no candidate passes, the rules' launch is used and the line says so.
transformations.lives: compiler process; result memoized in thread-local PICKS

transformations.name: Translate the site
transformations.plain: Reads the dataflow facts into placement's site.

transformations.name: Lower to check a candidate
to: Machine: emitted device text or refusal
transformations.plain: Turns the schedule into a launch and lowers the kernel text under a forced launch; with the ptxas arm it also assembles it and rejects spills.
transformations.lives: compiler process; the ptxas arm writes temp files and runs llc and ptxas

transformations.name: Record the pick
transformations.plain: Writes the chosen plan, times at three bounds, counters and terms into the module text.
transformations.lives: a comment line inside the emitted device module

transformations.name: Placement at launch time
transformations.plain: Called when the emitter derives a launch; returns the pick when the machine-place switch is on, else the rules' launch. A second entry picks the pick whose combine matches the kernel being emitted.
transformations.lives: compiler process; called from func/gpu.rs launch_in and launch_for

patterns.name: Branch and bound
patterns.plain: Search with an admissible lower bound that prunes prefixes and points.

patterns.name: Minimax regret over intervals
patterns.plain: Choose the candidate whose largest regret at any corner of the fact intervals is smallest.

patterns.name: Exact LRU trace simulation
patterns.plain: Counts misses of a line-granular LRU using a Fenwick tree over distinct bytes since last use.

patterns.name: Fenwick tree
patterns.plain: A binary indexed tree for prefix sums used by the LRU simulator.

patterns.name: Three-gap progression
patterns.plain: The gaps between readers of a row in a stream-K walk take at most three sizes; counted directly.

patterns.name: Closed-form reuse by interval unions
patterns.plain: Misses by distinct bytes over waves and walk windows, linear instead of simulated.

patterns.name: Memo caches in thread locals
patterns.plain: Pure functions of a grid are memoized in thread-local maps and cleared at a size cap.

patterns.name: Little's law flow
patterns.plain: A mover's time is the larger of work over rate and latency times work over bytes in flight.

patterns.name: Facts with intervals
patterns.plain: Every machine number has a low, value and high; evaluation at the ends makes uncertain picks visible.

patterns.name: Lowering as a trait
patterns.plain: The backend supplies its kernels as a Lowering that declares constraints and counts; the search is generic over them.

patterns.name: Incumbent with error band
patterns.plain: The rules' choice stays unless the model's pick beats it by more than the measured error band, so a re-measured rate does not churn emission.

patterns.name: Incumbent and candidate
patterns.plain: The rules' launch is always a point of the model's space, and wins unless beaten beyond the band.

patterns.name: Memo by search key
patterns.plain: A search is cached by site, part, face, arms and order in a thread-local map; related per-site memos are cleared when a search ends.

patterns.name: Scoped guards (RAII)
patterns.plain: WarmScope, ColScope and OrderScope set per-compile context and restore it when dropped.

patterns.name: Forced launch for lowering
patterns.plain: A thread-local FORCED launch replaces whatever the emitter would derive, so a candidate can be lowered and checked in isolation.

patterns.name: Plan and replay
patterns.plain: Measured arms are stored as data and every change is re-scored against them.

patterns.name: Coordinate domains
patterns.plain: A lowering's schedule space as a list of coordinates whose allowed values depend on earlier ones, so dominated choices are narrowed before the search.

components.name: LLVM backend
components.plain: Turns the Flow graph and its facts into LLVM text for the CPU and, for GPU programs, a device module that becomes PTX.

parts.name: Host code
parts.plain: Entry point and host function emission: loops, parallel tasks, CPU tiles.

parts.name: GPU memory residency
parts.plain: Which values live on the device, when they are copied or freed, and how device buffers share memory.

parts.name: GPU kernels
parts.plain: Kernels, the device module, and the table of candidate kernels a program picks from when it loads.

parts.name: Merged launches
parts.plain: Row-block units, one-pass streaming, merged launches and zero-fill folding.

parts.name: Switches and placement
parts.plain: How the rules' switches and the machine-model search reach the emitter.

transformations.name: emit_detailed
transformations.plain: The public entry: rebuilds facts under the fact arms asked for, resolves the profile, picks the face, then emits a host module (and a device module on GPU profiles).
transformations.lives: compiler process, pure over its inputs (profile is an explicit input)

transformations.name: emit_module
transformations.plain: Flow to LLVM IR text: checks loops are canonical, emits every function, adds only the declarations the text uses, and ends with the main wrapper.

transformations.name: FnEmit::emit_ordered
transformations.plain: One function: allocate slots, walk morphisms in topological order, then return and free.

transformations.name: emit_morphism
transformations.plain: The operation table: each Flow operation becomes its instructions, applied one morphism at a time.

transformations.name: emit_loop
transformations.plain: A canonical loop becomes guard-first branches: decide cone, branch, advance cone, back edge.

transformations.name: emit_parallel
transformations.plain: Splits independent paths into tasks launched on the mapal-rt pool and waits where the plan says.
transformations.lives: emitted code runs on host threads; handle on host heap

transformations.name: emit_tiled_map (tile ladder)
transformations.plain: Picks one CPU optimization switch for a matmul-like site: lanes, register block, packed panel, 1-D window, conv taps, or ARM SME.

transformations.name: emit_tiled_map_blocked
transformations.plain: Rows blocked in registers so one b load serves several rows.

transformations.name: emit_tiled_map_blocked_1d
transformations.plain: The dual for 1-D windows such as FIR: blocks over lanes.

transformations.name: emit_tiled_map_conv
transformations.plain: Conv micro-kernel with the k split constant-folded.

transformations.name: emit_tiled_map_sme
transformations.plain: ARM streaming matrix unit realization of a tile.

transformations.name: resident_plan
from: Facts: tile_plan, last_use_plan, path_plan, loop_plan, unchanged_plan, access_plan (Facts
transformations.plain: Reads the graph facts and decides placement for every object; no data is moved that the facts do not require.

transformations.name: placement
to: Code: device / host choice per site
transformations.plain: Per tile site: device or host, by the cost rules and the machine facts.

transformations.name: chains
to: Code: stream per site, uploads per chain
transformations.plain: Independent sites go on different streams; uploads ride the chain that reads them.

transformations.name: arena
transformations.plain: Lifetime colouring packs buffers into one slab.

transformations.name: color / color_by
transformations.plain: First-fit interval colouring.

transformations.name: emit_site_resident
to: Code: host calls: alloc, h2d, launch, d2h (Code)
transformations.plain: Emits the host-side calls that run one device site.
transformations.lives: emitted code runs on host; effects on GPU

transformations.name: row folds on device
transformations.plain: A row fold over a device output runs on the device, one thread per row, so the output never crosses the bus whole.

transformations.name: retained_sites
transformations.plain: Inside a loop recompute only the rows the previous trip wrote.

transformations.name: host-par
from: Code: split bulk sites on a GPU build
transformations.plain: Host-placed bulk work in a GPU build runs on the CPU task pool.

transformations.name: launch_in
transformations.plain: Chooses a kernel and its grid from the site and the hardware properties.

transformations.name: site_cands
transformations.plain: A table of candidate launches, the rules' choice first.

transformations.name: device_module
from: Code: Launch, cells, gens, epis, units, rowfolds
transformations.plain: Collects every live kernel and writes the nvptx module.

transformations.name: lowered_text / Kernel
transformations.plain: Writes one tile kernel: panel loops, FMA or matrix instructions, epilogue.

transformations.name: cell_kernel_text
transformations.plain: One thread per output cell, the host's own body text.

transformations.name: site_call
transformations.plain: Emits the host call with the table constant.

transformations.name: init_call
transformations.plain: First call of main: hands the runtime its flags after registering site tables.

transformations.name: opt then llc
transformations.plain: opt -O3 then llc for the profile's arch, with the declared PTX attribute.

transformations.name: load-time dispatch
transformations.plain: At module load the runtime resolves each table to one candidate from shared-memory limits and occupancy.

transformations.name: unit_of (flow)
transformations.plain: A consumer joins its producer's group when everything it reads from the producer lies in the same work unit, or is a halo the group recomputes.

transformations.name: block_choice / geo
transformations.plain: Rows per block and the resource budget from registers, shared memory and the roofline of fused versus separate launches.

transformations.name: unit_kernel
transformations.plain: One kernel for the group: members in order as phases, values kept in registers or shared memory unless a reader outside needs them.

transformations.name: stream_geo
transformations.plain: Walks one axis in windows with running max and sum so axis-wide values are never stored.

transformations.name: mma_fmt
transformations.plain: Whether every product in the stream fits one warp matrix instruction.

transformations.name: side_by_side
transformations.plain: Whether launches with no hazard between them fit one grid at no loss in waves.

transformations.name: hz_launch
transformations.plain: Captures each member's launch and issues the group after its last member.

transformations.name: persistent_fit / chain_ns
to: Code: grid size or Refuse; time
transformations.plain: A chain is one co-resident kernel when it fits and beats separate launches.

transformations.name: zero-fold / zero-hoist
transformations.plain: A zero pass becomes extra stores in an earlier kernel, or is issued after the earliest step that allows it.

transformations.name: rules::optimization switches
transformations.plain: Each optimization switch decides from properties such as FFMA per DRAM byte, registers per thread, L2 per SM.

transformations.name: arms applied over rules
transformations.plain: on forces, off removes; default arms are empty.

transformations.name: placed (machine-place search)
transformations.plain: A cost model over candidate lowerings picks a launch; a pick that does not clear the band keeps the rules' launch. Off by default.

transformations.name: machine_of
transformations.plain: Profile facts become machine facts with source and spread.

transformations.name: profile::resolve
transformations.plain: Detects the host (sysfs, sysctl) or device (driver query plus calibration) and returns a static profile.

patterns.name: Slot per object, mem2reg left to LLVM
patterns.plain: Every value gets a stack cell written once; LLVM turns them into registers.

patterns.name: Guard-first loop CFG
patterns.plain: The loop header decides first, so the exit trip still runs the decide cone.

patterns.name: Fixpoint over the call graph (attribute capability)
patterns.plain: A function is clean only if every callee is clean; loops block willreturn.

patterns.name: Arena of typed ids (SecondaryMap)
patterns.plain: Per-object and per-morphism side tables keyed by slotmap ids.

patterns.name: Declare only what is used
patterns.plain: Runtime declarations are added by searching the emitted text for the call.

patterns.name: Strategy ladder with a predicate per optimization switch
patterns.plain: Each CPU tile optimization switch has one test (packing_site, window1d_site, conv_site, sme_tile_site) and one emitter.

patterns.name: Loop buffer colouring
patterns.plain: Next-state bytes take a spare buffer not read while they are written.

patterns.name: Text builder as the artifact
patterns.plain: The String is the translation unit; no intermediate LLVM object model.

patterns.name: Plan then replay
patterns.plain: A pure plan record is computed first; emission only reads it.

patterns.name: First-fit interval colouring
patterns.plain: Buffers with disjoint lifetimes share bytes.

patterns.name: Delta transfer
patterns.plain: Only the rows a trip wrote are uploaded or recomputed.

patterns.name: Lazy allocation through a slot
patterns.plain: The runtime fills the slot on first use, so the host emits no branch.

patterns.name: Candidate table, chosen at load
patterns.plain: Compile time lists launches; the runtime picks one from device limits.

patterns.name: Content-hashed kernel ids
patterns.plain: FNV hash of body and profile names a kernel so equal kernels merge.

patterns.name: Rule table over hardware properties
patterns.plain: Choices read geometry (SMs, registers, L2, bandwidth), never a part name.

patterns.name: Stream-K / split-K
patterns.plain: Cut the k fold across blocks, add partials atomically or via workspace.

patterns.name: Software-pipelined panels
patterns.plain: Next panel loads while this one computes (cp.async, TMA).

patterns.name: Footprint rule (producer cells read lie inside the unit)
patterns.plain: Group membership is decided only by what each work unit reads, not by an operator name.

patterns.name: Online softmax / running rescale
patterns.plain: A running maximum and sum are rescaled as windows arrive.

patterns.name: Tree and warp-shuffle reduction
patterns.plain: Row totals by tree in shared memory or by shuffles.

patterns.name: Hazard graph (RAW/WAR/WAW) as the merge test
patterns.plain: Launches merge only if the access plan leaves them unordered.

patterns.name: Grid barrier
patterns.plain: A level barrier inside a persistent kernel.

patterns.name: Ticket (last block combines)
patterns.plain: The last block to finish a row combines partial states.

patterns.name: Plan + replay
patterns.plain: Rules are checked by replaying every cited measurement.

patterns.name: ON/OFF measurement arms
patterns.plain: Every optimization switch has an off arm for A/B; defaults come from rules, not flags.

patterns.name: Roofline cost
patterns.plain: Time is the larger of flops over rate and bytes over bandwidth.

patterns.name: Candidate search with admissible floor
patterns.plain: The search prunes candidates whose lower bound cannot beat the best.

patterns.name: Memoization by key (thread-local)
patterns.plain: Searches and machines are cached per key inside one emission.

components.name: CUDA backend
components.plain: A second backend that writes CUDA C for the same graph, used as a differential check against the main backend.

transformations.name: emit_with_opts
transformations.plain: Flow to .cu text, deterministic, with only the non-canonical loop shape unsupported.

transformations.name: emit_kernel_set
transformations.plain: One kernel per structural shape; each site launches it.

transformations.name: emit_loop
transformations.plain: Decide, guard, advance, back edge; in-place updates where the last-use plan allows.

transformations.name: arena_plan
transformations.plain: Give every non-loop buffer the next aligned offset.

transformations.name: nvcc compile and run
transformations.plain: Built on a GPU box and linked with mapal-rt.
transformations.lives: external nvcc; files on the box

patterns.name: Shape-deduplicated kernels
patterns.plain: One definition per structural shape, launched from many sites.

patterns.name: Capability fixpoint (TrapCaps)
patterns.plain: A launch may trap if any reachable callee may.

patterns.name: Fn-scope arena zone
patterns.plain: One allocation and one release per function, escape-checked.

patterns.name: Host-driven loop
patterns.plain: The loop runs on the host; each trip launches kernels.

components.name: Verilog backend
components.plain: Not built yet: the crate is a one-line placeholder.

components.name: Runtime
components.plain: The code a compiled program links against: host memory, parallel tasks, printing and traps, and the GPU driver glue (with a CPU emulator of the device).

transformations.name: Run a parallel region
transformations.plain: The emitted program builds a task graph with begin, task and dep calls; launch seals it and queues slices; workers run them; wait and finish join. Any trap inside a task is reported in program order.
transformations.lives: host threads of the global Pool; frame shared through Run.frame

transformations.name: Build the graph
transformations.plain: Collect tasks and edges while the program issues them.

transformations.name: Seal
transformations.plain: Turn the mutable build list into immutable tasks with atomic counters.

transformations.name: Slice and queue
transformations.plain: Cut each ready task into slices (size from the grain, the pool width and MAPAL_SLICE) and put them on lane queues.

transformations.name: Worker loop
transformations.plain: Each worker takes from its own queue, steals from others, runs the slice, and when a task's last slice finishes releases its dependents.

transformations.name: Wait and finish
transformations.plain: The caller helps run work until its tasks are done, then checks for a trap.

transformations.name: Allocate host memory
transformations.plain: Whole-program blocks come from a global list freed at the end; per-call blocks come from a per-thread stack released on return.

transformations.name: Print and trap
transformations.plain: A print writes the shortest round-trip text and flushes. A trap prints 'mapal trap: div_zero|index_oob' and exits 101.

transformations.name: Load the device module
transformations.plain: On a helper thread: start the driver, make the context, load the PTX, resolve all kernels and the site tables. The first site call joins it.
transformations.lives: helper pthread then host heap and the GPU context

transformations.name: Move bytes
transformations.plain: Allocate, upload, download and free by the emitted program's explicit calls; the runtime adds no copy of its own.

transformations.name: Launch a kernel
transformations.plain: Look up the kernel by id, set its shared memory limit, enqueue on the stream the emitter named.
transformations.lives: driver call cuLaunchKernel; arguments built on the host stack

transformations.name: Pick a candidate for a site
transformations.plain: Use the forced index, the stored winner, a timed trial of every candidate, or the compiler's first one, in that order; remember the answer.
transformations.lives: trial timed with events on the device; result appended to the wisdom file

transformations.name: Carry a device trap to the host
transformations.plain: A kernel writes the word; the next host print, clock, copy-back or exit reads it and raises the same trap the host would.
transformations.lives: the hook is a function pointer in the Rust runtime's CHECKPOINT atomic

transformations.name: Emulate the device on the CPU
transformations.plain: Same entry points, device memory is host memory and a kernel is run once per thread, so tests can check the host half without a GPU.
transformations.lives: host heap filled with 0xA5; blocks run as threads that meet at barrier functions

patterns.name: Task graph with dependency counters
patterns.plain: Each task counts unmet dependencies; at zero it becomes ready.

patterns.name: Work-stealing pool with spin then park
patterns.plain: Per-lane queues; idle workers steal, spin briefly, then sleep on a condition variable.

patterns.name: Epoch counter plus condition variable
patterns.plain: A counter bumped on every change lets waiters re-check without missing a wake-up.

patterns.name: Build then seal
patterns.plain: A mutable list while being built, an immutable lock-free array afterwards.

patterns.name: Arena with one teardown
patterns.plain: Allocate often, free everything once; per-call frames use a mark and release stack.

patterns.name: Pure-function parsing of quotas
patterns.plain: Thread count from MAPAL_PAR and cgroup limits is computed by small pure functions so it can be tested.

patterns.name: Autotune with memo and persistent cache (plan then replay)
patterns.plain: Time every candidate once, store the winner keyed by a hash of the table and module, never time again.

patterns.name: FNV-1a hash
patterns.plain: The key of a site decision.

patterns.name: Direct-mapped memo by table address
patterns.plain: A decided site costs one pointer compare.

patterns.name: Init on a helper thread, join at first use
patterns.plain: Driver start-up overlaps with host work before the first site.

patterns.name: Kernel lookup by id with preloaded table
patterns.plain: A hash table from kernel id to function handle built from the PTX text.

patterns.name: Stream join by events
patterns.plain: A chain stream waits on an event recorded on the default stream if anything was enqueued there since its last join.

patterns.name: Deferred trap checkpoint
patterns.plain: The device error is read only at points where the host would observe a value.

patterns.name: Baton scheduling in the emulator
patterns.plain: Cooperative blocks run one at a time and hand over at grid barriers; a barrier that never completes exits 105.

components.name: Command line
components.plain: The `mapal` command: it runs the stages in order for build, run, test, dump-ir, fmt, repl and lsp.

transformations.name: frontend (source to checked IR)
transformations.plain: parse, then lower, then check; any diagnostic stops with exit 1.

transformations.name: parse
transformations.plain: Source text to parse tree.

transformations.name: lower
transformations.plain: Parse tree to the IR; also records the source directory.

transformations.name: check
transformations.plain: Rules on effects and exclusivity.

transformations.name: rewritten (static folding then rewrite)
transformations.plain: Compute what is known before the run, then apply the rewrite rules.

transformations.name: emit
transformations.plain: Plan and write LLVM text for host and device.

transformations.name: build (emit, tools, link)
transformations.plain: Write <exe>.ll; on a GPU profile run opt -O3 and llc -O3 for the card's arch to get PTX, compile the host with clang, write the C GPU runtime next to it and link it with libcuda; on CPU link the .ll with libmapal_rt.a.
transformations.lives: child processes opt, llc, clang; files on disk

transformations.name: Write host .ll
transformations.plain: Save the host text.

transformations.name: Optimize device IR
transformations.plain: opt -O3.

transformations.name: Device IR to PTX
transformations.plain: llc -O3 with -mcpu from the profile's GPU arch and -mattr from the module's declared PTX version.

transformations.name: Compile host object (GPU)
transformations.plain: clang -O2 -c.

transformations.name: Link
transformations.plain: clang links host, runtime library, and on GPU the C runtime with -lcuda from MAPAL_CUDA.

transformations.name: run
transformations.plain: Compile into a temp directory, run the program (with MAPAL_PTX set on GPU), pass through its exit code, delete the directory. With --interp: run the interpreter instead.

transformations.name: in_temp
transformations.plain: Make the temp directory, build, give the executable command to a closure, remove the directory.

transformations.name: dump-ir
transformations.plain: Print the IR at a chosen stage (lowered, rewritten, llvm, device) or as a Mermaid diagram.

transformations.name: test
transformations.plain: Run the interpreter with the compiled program's fold orders and the compiled program with a timeout, and compare exit code and output byte for byte (or against the composed bound when a product admits a weaker member).
transformations.lives: child process stdout through a pipe, read by wait_boxed

transformations.name: Interpreter run (oracle)
transformations.plain: run, run_ordered, run_weakest or run_bound, then native_observable.

transformations.name: fmt
transformations.plain: Format files in place, check, or print to stdout; rejects invalid input.

transformations.name: repl
transformations.plain: Keep each definition and statement; on each input rebuild the whole program from the session and run it on the interpreter, showing only the new output.
transformations.lives: compiler heap; history file on disk

transformations.name: lsp
transformations.plain: Start the language server on stdin and stdout.

patterns.name: Pipeline of stages with a single error type
patterns.plain: Each stage returns Result<_, u8> with the exit code; the message is already printed.

patterns.name: Artifacts named after the executable
patterns.plain: Every side file is <exe><ext>.

patterns.name: Embedded runtime source
patterns.plain: The C runtime is compiled into the CLI with include_str! and written out at build time, so the build needs only the CLI and the toolchain.

patterns.name: Temporary build directory
patterns.plain: A private folder per process, removed even on failure.

patterns.name: Differential testing against an oracle
patterns.plain: The interpreter is the specification; test_cmd checks the native program against it.

patterns.name: Timeout by polling a child
patterns.plain: Run the program with piped stdout and kill it after N seconds.

patterns.name: Replay session in REPL
patterns.plain: State is the list of inputs, not a running machine.

patterns.name: Toolchain lookup by environment
patterns.plain: CC, LLVM, MAPAL_RT, MAPAL_CUDA, MAPAL_LD select the tools; missing tools exit 3.

components.name: Language server and editors
components.plain: Gives editors the compiler's own answers (errors, hover, go to definition, rename, colors) and ships the Neovim and VS Code plugins.

transformations.name: Analysis::new
transformations.plain: Parses and lexes the text, then walks the tree with a stack of scopes to record every definition and use, each with a role and highlight class.

transformations.name: compile_diagnostics
transformations.plain: Runs the compiler's front end (parse, then lower and check if the parse is clean) and returns the same errors `mapal build` would, turning a front-end crash into a warning.
transformations.lives: a worker thread with a 64 MiB stack, fed by a channel that keeps only the newest text per document

transformations.name: serve (the request loop)
transformations.plain: Reads requests and notifications from the editor over stdin/stdout, keeps open documents, answers definition, references, hover, symbols, rename, completion, format and semantic tokens, and pushes diagnostics.
transformations.lives: main server thread; messages are JSON over stdio

transformations.name: mapal lsp command
transformations.plain: The CLI subcommand that starts the server on stdin/stdout.
transformations.lives: an OS process started by the editor

transformations.name: encode_tokens
transformations.plain: Turns the classified spans into the editor's delta-encoded semantic token array.
transformations.lives: server heap: Vec<SemanticToken> in the reply

transformations.name: Neovim starts the server
transformations.plain: On opening a .mapal file, runs `mapal lsp` (command overridable by a global setting) through vim.lsp.config / vim.lsp.start.
transformations.lives: a child OS process talking over stdio

transformations.name: VS Code starts the server
transformations.plain: The extension finds the executable (setting, bundled binary, or PATH) and launches `<executable> lsp` over stdio; formatting falls back to `<executable> fmt -`.
transformations.lives: extension host process spawning a child process

transformations.name: format on request
transformations.plain: The editors send buffer text to the formatter (through the server or `mapal fmt -`) and replace the buffer.
transformations.lives: buffer text in the editor, formatter in the mapal process

patterns.name: Pure analysis, rebuilt per edit
patterns.plain: Analysis depends only on the text; no incremental state to keep in sync.

patterns.name: Scope-frame stack walker
patterns.plain: The walker pushes a frame per function, block and loop, binds names into it, and looks names up from the inner frame outward.

patterns.name: Definition table plus occurrence list
patterns.plain: Definitions are in one vector and every use points to one by index, so references and rename need no search of the tree.

patterns.name: Background worker with coalescing queue
patterns.plain: Diagnostics run on their own thread, and a burst of edits to one document collapses to the latest.

patterns.name: UTF-16 position mapping
patterns.plain: Editors count columns in UTF-16 units while the compiler counts bytes, so a line table converts between them.

patterns.name: Request dispatch by method name
patterns.plain: One match routes each protocol method to a handler.

patterns.name: Single class table checked by three tests
patterns.plain: One table drives tests in Neovim, VS Code and the server crate so they cannot drift.

patterns.name: Layered highlighting (static grammar, then server tokens)
patterns.plain: The grammar gives instant colours; the server's semantic tokens refine names once it is running.

patterns.name: Executable discovery order
patterns.plain: Setting first, bundled binary second, PATH last.

guarantees.name: The lowered graph means what the program means
guarantees.plain: For every program, interpreting the lowered graph gives what interpreting the parse tree gives.
guarantees.note: Checked on example programs run on the interpreter; the generated-program test checks only that lowering gives valid graphs, not yet that they agree with the tree's meaning.

guarantees.name: Formatting keeps the tree
guarantees.plain: Parsing the formatted text gives the same tree as parsing the original (apart from positions), and formatting twice changes nothing.

guarantees.name: Lexing and parsing never fail
guarantees.plain: For every input string, even invalid, lexing and parsing return a result and never panic; bad input shows up only as diagnostics.
paths: parse the text in one step

guarantees.name: Accepted means the interpreter's assumptions hold
guarantees.plain: For every program the checker accepts, what the interpreter assumes (one return writer, no effect racing in a fan-out) is true.

guarantees.name: Editor errors equal build errors
guarantees.plain: For every file, the errors the editor shows are the errors the compiler's own front end gives.
paths: compiler front end: parse, lower, check

guarantees.name: Rename keeps meaning
guarantees.plain: Renaming a definition edits exactly its occurrences, so every name still resolves to the same definition.
guarantees.note: The two paths are: rename then resolve, and resolve then rename the table's keys.

guarantees.name: Same highlighting everywhere
guarantees.plain: For each highlight class, Vim, TextMate and the server's tokens give the same look, with or without the server running.
guarantees.note: editors/test.sh is the gate that holds the Vim and TextMate files to the same class table.

guarantees.name: Facts agree with the interpreter
guarantees.plain: A claim a fact makes (a tile bound, a proven index, a static value) holds when the interpreter runs the program.
guarantees.note: Similar checks are spread over several rewrite tests; these two are the closest.

guarantees.name: Rewrite preserves the interpreter's result
guarantees.plain: Evaluating the graph before and after rewriting gives the same result, traps included.

guarantees.name: Replaying nothing changes nothing
guarantees.plain: Replaying with an empty plan reproduces a valid graph equal to the original for every example.

guarantees.name: Rewrite is deterministic and idempotent
guarantees.plain: Rewriting twice equals rewriting once, and the same input always gives the same output.

guarantees.name: A sealed graph is always valid
guarantees.plain: Every program the builder accepts passes validation, and every rule validate has has a matching rejection in the builder.

guarantees.name: Pictures are stable
guarantees.plain: Every example graph draws to byte-identical Mermaid text (stored snapshots) and passes the lint.

guarantees.name: Graph algorithms agree with loop structure
guarantees.plain: Every loop is exactly one non-trivial cycle holding its merge, and loop-back edges are exactly the cycle breakers.

guarantees.name: Same graph, same result
guarantees.plain: Running twice gives the identical outcome and output (no hash maps, no clocks in the value path).

guarantees.name: The default face lies inside the bound
guarantees.plain: The weakest-precision run differs from the exact run by at most the composed error bound.

guarantees.name: Traps and divergence are outcomes, not panics
guarantees.plain: An out-of-range index, a zero division or running out of steps gives Trapped or Diverged rather than a crash.
paths: name the outcome: ok, trapped or diverged

guarantees.name: Compiled code agrees with the interpreter within the bound
guarantees.plain: The compiled program's printed values equal the interpreter's within the interpreter's bound; the check lives in the backend tests.
guarantees.note: Checked in the LLVM backend's tests, not in the interpreter's.

guarantees.name: Emulator agrees with the device
guarantees.plain: The emulated entry points and the real ones give the same values and the same trap outcome; both share the same pick code.
guarantees.note: Stated, not checked by a test here: these tests check the emulator against the interpreter; the real device is compared on a GPU box.

guarantees.name: Print agrees with the interpreter
guarantees.plain: Compiled and interpreted programs print the same text, because both use the same formatter and trap codes.

guarantees.name: A compiled run agrees with the interpreter
guarantees.plain: Emitting, linking and running gives the same output and exit code as the interpreter on the fixed face, and the same within the bound otherwise. `mapal test` is the gate.

guarantees.name: Rewrite and no-rewrite agree
guarantees.plain: The --no-rewrite arm and the default arm give the same result; both stay reachable for A/B checks.

guarantees.name: The native profile is the query plus the calibration
guarantees.plain: For every device query and calibration line, the native profile equals the one built from those two inputs alone (no name lookup).
paths: build by hand from the same two inputs

guarantees.name: The rules agree with every cited measurement
guarantees.plain: For every recorded measurement, what the rules decide matches the measured winner, or the line is marked open.

guarantees.name: The rules ignore names
guarantees.plain: Two parts with the same properties take the same switches.

guarantees.name: Search equals exhaustive
guarantees.plain: For every machine and site, branch and bound finds the same best time as pricing every candidate.

guarantees.name: The closed form equals the LRU simulation
guarantees.plain: For lockstep grids the closed form equals the exact cache simulation byte for byte; for walks and staggers it is within a slice or five percent.

guarantees.name: Time is monotone and above the bound
guarantees.plain: A faster machine or a smaller site never raises the price, and the price is never below the admissible bound.

guarantees.name: The pick does not depend on enumeration order
guarantees.plain: Reversing every domain gives the same pick, and noise flips only picks marked open.

guarantees.name: The pick agrees with the measured winner
guarantees.plain: For every row of the replay corpus the model's pick is scored against the measured winner and the rules' pick; the count of agreements may not fall.

guarantees.name: The floor is admissible on every replay arm
guarantees.plain: For every replayed arm, the cheap floor is never above the full price.

guarantees.name: The host launches the kernel the device module holds
guarantees.plain: The host launches exactly the kernel the device module contains, including when the pick is kept.

guarantees.name: The error band is the replay's residuals
guarantees.plain: The error band written in the compiler equals the one recomputed from the replay data.

guarantees.name: A native run agrees with the interpreter
guarantees.plain: Compile and run gives the interpreter's output and exit status, at -O0 and -O2, on raw and rewritten graphs.

guarantees.name: Emission is deterministic
guarantees.plain: The same graph and options always give the same text; stored snapshots pin it.

guarantees.name: Data movement equals what the facts require
guarantees.plain: The copies and allocations emitted are exactly those the dataflow facts need.

guarantees.name: The device agrees with the interpreter within the bound
guarantees.plain: GPU results equal the interpreter's inside the stated error bound.
paths: emit and run on the GPU
guarantees.note: Device kernels run through the CPU emulator in these tests; real GPUs are compared on rented boxes.

guarantees.name: A switch on and off compute the same values
guarantees.plain: Each switch only moves operands; turning it off changes speed, not values.

guarantees.name: A merged launch equals separate launches
guarantees.plain: A merged group gives the same values as its members launched alone.

guarantees.name: Streamed attention agrees with the interpreter
guarantees.plain: The one-pass attention kernel matches the interpreter within the bound.

guarantees.name: A CUDA run agrees with the interpreter
guarantees.plain: Outputs and traps equal the interpreter's.
paths: emit CUDA, compile with nvcc, run

guarantees.name: CUDA emission is deterministic
guarantees.plain: Stored .cu snapshots pin the text.

operations.name: Pair
operations.plain: Puts a value into slot i of a product of n slots.

operations.name: Proj
operations.plain: Takes component i out of a product.

operations.name: Add
operations.plain: Adds the two numbers of its pair.

operations.name: Sub
operations.plain: Subtracts.

operations.name: Mul
operations.plain: Multiplies.

operations.name: Div
operations.plain: Divides (a zero integer divisor traps).

operations.name: Mod
operations.plain: Remainder.

operations.name: Neg
operations.plain: Negates a number.

operations.name: Eq
operations.plain: Equal.

operations.name: Neq
operations.plain: Not equal.

operations.name: Lt
operations.plain: Less than.

operations.name: Gt
operations.plain: Greater than.

operations.name: Le
operations.plain: At most.

operations.name: Ge
operations.plain: At least.

operations.name: And
operations.plain: Both true.

operations.name: Or
operations.plain: Either true.

operations.name: Not
operations.plain: Negates a truth value.

operations.name: Phi
operations.plain: Picks one of two values by a condition: the coproduct (guard) of two branches.

operations.name: Call
operations.plain: Calls a named function.

operations.name: Map
operations.plain: Applies a function body to every element (with optional captured values broadcast to all).

operations.name: Fold
operations.plain: Folds an array into one value from a start value with a function body.

operations.name: Index
operations.plain: Reads one element of an array; out of range traps.

operations.name: Zip
operations.plain: Pairs two arrays of the same length element by element.

operations.name: Enumerate
operations.plain: Pairs every element with its index.

operations.name: Iota
operations.plain: The array 0, 1, ..., n-1.

operations.name: Fill
operations.plain: An array of n copies of one value.

operations.name: Update
operations.plain: A copy of an array with one element replaced.

operations.name: Print
operations.plain: Prints a value and passes the token on.

operations.name: TimeMs
operations.plain: Reads the clock; gives the next token and the milliseconds.

operations.name: Read
operations.plain: Reads a file into an array; gives the next token and the array.

operations.name: LoopEnter
operations.plain: Feeds the loop's start value into the loop state.

operations.name: LoopBack
operations.plain: The back edge: sends the next state to the loop state when the condition says continue.

operations.name: LoopExit
operations.plain: Sends the loop state out when the condition says stop.

operations.name: Output
operations.plain: Sends a value to the function's return.

operations.name: Widen

operations.name: Narrow
operations.plain: Rounds once to a narrow float format (bf16, f16).

operations.name: Math
operations.plain: A math builtin on a float: exp, sqrt, sin or cos.

notes.name: Products
notes.plain: Several values held together are one object, a product. Pair builds it, Proj takes a part out, and every binary operation reads a pair.

notes.name: Coproducts (guards)
notes.plain: A choice between two branches is a coproduct: Phi picks one value by a condition, and the facts record which work belongs to which arm.

notes.name: Loops (traced feedback)
notes.plain: A loop is a cycle in the graph: LoopEnter feeds the start value into the loop state, LoopBack feeds the next state back, and LoopExit leaves. There is no loop node.
